title: No one belongs to Christ who does not keep the commandments
source_text: IX. Neque vero quisquam est in communione Christi, aut eum vere nosse & amare censeri potest, qui mandata Dei non servet. In hoc scimus, inquit Johannes, quoniam cognovimus eum, si mandata ejus observamus. Qui dicit se nosse Deum, & mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est, & veritas in eo non est. 1 Joan. 2. & cap. 3. Qui servat mandata ejus in illo manet, & ipse in eo. Similiter cap. 5. Haec est charitas Dei ut mandata ejus custodiamus. Unde est quod Paulus, 1 Cor. 7. solam observationem mandatorum Dei alicujus momenti in Christo esse docet, Circumcisio, inquit, nihil est: & praeputium nihil est: sed observatio mandatorum Dei.
pass_a_gloss: IX. Nor indeed is anyone in communion with Christ, or can he be judged truly to know & love him, who does not keep the commandments of God. In this we know, says John, that we have known him, if we observe his commandments. He who says he knows God, & does not keep his commandments, is a liar, & the truth is not in him. 1 John 2. & chap. 3. He who keeps his commandments abides in him, & he in him. Likewise chap. 5. This is the charity of God that we keep his commandments. Whence it is that Paul, 1 Cor. 7. teaches that only the observance of the commandments of God is of any moment in Christ, Circumcision, he says, is nothing: & uncircumcision is nothing: but the observance of the commandments of God.
pass_b_english: Thesis IX. No one who fails to keep God's commandments is in communion with Christ or can be thought truly to know and love him. John says: 'By this we know that we have known him, if we keep his commandments. Whoever says he knows God but does not keep his commandments is a liar, and the truth is not in him' (1 John 2).

In chapter 3: 'Whoever keeps his commandments remains in him, and he in him'; and in chapter 5: 'This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments.' That is why Paul (1 Cor. 7) teaches that in Christ nothing counts for anything but keeping God's commandments: 'Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing; what counts is keeping the commandments of God.'

lemmas.gloss: the observance of the commandments of God

choices.why: Scripture's phrase for the obedience of believers, kept distinct from perfect fulfilment of the law.
